newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia in deals for 1.3 mln tonnes Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Russia in deals for 1.3 mln tonnes Iraqi oil.

text.p: Three Russian oil companies have signed contracts with Iraq to buy 1.3 million tonnes (roughly 9.62 million barrels) of Iraqi crude oil and are awaiting U.N. approval, a Russian official involved in the deal said on Tuesday.
Yuri Agababov, deputy head of Zarubezhneft, was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying his firm, NK LUKoil and Nafta-Moskva had signed deals on Sunday in Baghdad.

Under the deal, Zarubezhneft would buy 500,000 tonnes (3.7 million barrels) of crude over six months. The two other companies would each lift 400,000 tonnes (2.96 million barrels) over the same period.
Agababov, the coordinator of the deals, said he expected liftings to begin before January 10.
The Russians submitted their contracts to United Nations officials on Monday and expected approval within 24 hours.

Iraq began exporting oil for the first time in six years on December 16 from the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan under a deal with the United Nations in which Baghdad will sell $2 billion worth of crude over six months on a renewal basis for food and medicine.
